name: Marlowe Arrieta
life: “I still remember learning the difference between my doctor's real laugh and her polite one.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the blocks below Foundry Lofts, where Marlowe checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I asked for a last appointment to talk about anything other than my illness. We got halfway through comparing bad films.
appearance: Marlowe has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for auburn hair cut square at the nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a pale blue work shirt with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Marlowe counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Marlowe takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Marlowe can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To finish the conversation about bad films.
family: Frances Brady is Marlowe’s second cousin. Marlowe asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Frances remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The widow's dividend*, Frances says, “I sold my shares for a taxi license. I still own the pen that signed them away.”
connections: Gavin Kang. A portrait of a tattoo and a conversation about movies offer two goodbyes outside illness.

reactions.response: Marlowe gives the new doctor a chance to speak before retelling the old doctor's habits.
